# ezghcloud_firewall (Resource)

Manage a firewall and its complete set of rules. Do not manage the same firewall's rules with another resource or tool.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Resource name.
- `project_id` (String) Project owning this resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Firewall description.
- `rules` (Attributes Set) Complete owned rule collection. Omitted or [] means no rules; no automatic outbound rules are added. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `tags` (Map of String) Customer resource tags.

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Strong service version used for conditional rule replacement.
- `id` (String) Canonical prefixed resource ID.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization owning this resource.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `status` (String) Current service status.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `direction` (String) inbound or outbound.
- `protocol` (String) tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, all, or another IANA protocol number as a string. Use named forms for 6, 17, 1 and 58.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Rule description.
- `icmp_code` (Number) ICMP code (0–255); omit for every code of the selected type.
- `icmp_type` (Number) ICMP type (0–255); omit for every type.
- `peer_cidr` (String) Canonical IPv4 or IPv6 peer prefix. Exactly one peer selector is required.
- `peer_database_id` (String) Peer database ID (dbi_) in this project: traffic to and from it. Exactly one peer selector is required.
- `peer_firewall_id` (String) Peer firewall ID. Exactly one peer selector is required.
- `ports_from` (Number) First TCP/UDP port (1–65535); omit both port fields for all ports.
- `ports_to` (Number) Last TCP/UDP port (1–65535).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_firewall.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/RESOURCE_ID'
```
